Chapter 9: Emotional Clutter—Letting Go of Guilt, Sentiment, and “Someday”
You know, when we think about clutter, it’s easy to picture all the stuff piling up around the house. But often, there’s something deeper going on—emotional clutter. Maybe you’ve got things tucked away because you feel guilty getting rid of them, or you’re hanging on to souvenirs from the past, or even holding onto things for that elusive “someday.” These objects can weigh on us, making it tough to create a space that actually feels calm and welcoming.
So, how do we start untangling this emotional mess? It helps to gently ask yourself some honest questions. Pick up something that stirs up memories or tugs at your heart—maybe a gift from a loved one, a keepsake from long ago, or something tied to who you used to be. Now, pause and ask: Does this support who I am, right now? Or am I just keeping it because I feel I should?
Let’s talk about a few ways to make letting go a little easier:
First, try thanking the item. Sounds simple, but acknowledging what it’s meant to you—before you let it go—can bring a real sense of closure.
Another idea? Take a photo of sentimental things. You still get to keep the memory, but you’re free from the physical clutter.
And if you’re on the fence, set a limit for “maybe” items. Put them in a box and promise yourself you’ll check back in a few months. Chances are, you’ll realize you don’t actually need most of it.
It’s totally normal to feel a little resistance as you go through this. Don’t beat yourself up. Sit with those feelings, talk them through with a friend, or even write them down. Sometimes, just naming what you’re feeling brings a lot of clarity.
Now, let’s talk about guilt. That’s a big one, especially with gifts or things you’ve inherited. But here’s the thing—your home is for you, not for living up to someone else’s expectations. Letting go of an item doesn’t erase its meaning or your relationship with the person who gave it to you.
Then there’s the classic “someday” trap. We all have those things we’re keeping just in case. But ask yourself—when was the last time you actually used it? If it’s been years, it’s probably safe to let it go and reclaim that space, both physically and mentally.
Remember, this isn’t a one-and-done project. Letting go is a journey, not a sprint. Start small, and celebrate each choice you make. Every little step brings you closer to a home—and mind—that feels lighter and more peaceful.
